HTTP.d: Hypertext Transfer Protocol: the set of rules programs use to send requests and responses over the web. HTTPS is the encrypted version.

JSON.d: JavaScript Object Notation: a plain-text format for structured data using objects { }, lists [ ], text in double quotes, numbers, true/false and null. Most APIs send and receive JSON.

Endpoint.d: A specific address an API offers, written as a method plus a path, such as POST /v1/messages.

Header.d: A short Name: value line sent with an HTTP request or response that describes it, such as Content-Type or Authorization.

Status code.d: The three-digit number at the start of an HTTP response saying how the request went: 2xx success, 4xx a problem with the request, 5xx a problem on the server.

Rate limit.d: A cap on how much you can use an API in a period of time. Going over it returns 429 Too Many Requests.

Webhook.d: A request a service sends to a URL you provide when an event happens, so you don't have to keep asking whether something changed.

curl.d: A command-line program for sending HTTP requests. Most API documentation shows its examples as curl commands.

REST.d: A common style of web API that uses URLs for things (resources) and HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) for actions on them.

API key.d: A long secret string that identifies a program to an API. Anyone holding it can act as you, so it must be kept like a password.

SDK.d: Software development kit: a ready-made library that makes calling an API easier, handling headers, retries and errors for you. Anthropic publishes SDKs for Python, TypeScript and other languages.
